slides.title: School Kitchen Garden
bullets: Class 6 — CBSE Vocational Education
Kaushal Bodh — Chapter 1
slides.speaker_notes: From seed to plate, right at school.

slides.title: What you'll be able to do
bullets: Define a kitchen garden + 3 benefits.
Pick a spot and a season-appropriate crop.
Use simple tools safely.
Compare direct sowing, seedlings, cuttings.
Care for plants daily and weekly.
Plan a small garden layout.

slides.title: What is a kitchen garden?
bullets: A small garden of plants you can eat.
Different from a flower garden or a forest.
Can be 5 pots — or a school plot.
Plants need: soil, water, sunlight, air, care.
Benefits: fresh food, learning, pollinators, friendships.

slides.title: Plan first — pick the spot
bullets: At least 4–6 hours of sunlight per day.
Close to a water source.
Away from heavy footfall.
Sketch a layout on paper.
Tall plants behind, short in front.

slides.title: Three Indian growing seasons
bullets: KHARIF — sown Jun/Jul with monsoon. Gourds, brinjal, beans.
RABI — sown Oct/Nov. Spinach, coriander, peas, radish.
ZAID — sown Mar/Apr. Cucumber, watermelon.
Match the crop to the season for best results.
Different parts of India shift these dates a little.

slides.title: What can a Class 6 grow?
bullets: Tomato, brinjal, chilli (seedlings).
Lady's finger (direct).
Spinach, coriander (direct).
Mint, curry leaves (cuttings).
Tulsi in a pot near the door.

slides.title: Tools and materials
bullets: Khurpi — small hand-hoe; for digging and weeding.
Trowel — for transplanting seedlings.
Watering can — for gentle watering.
Soil + compost in 2:1 ratio.
Mulch (dry leaves), stakes, gloves, wooden tags.

slides.title: Three ways to start a plant
bullets: DIRECT sowing — seed straight into bed (spinach, coriander, radish).
SEEDLINGS — start in tray, transplant later (tomato, brinjal, chilli).
CUTTINGS — stem grows roots in moist soil (mint, curry leaves).
Seeds need: moisture + warmth + time.
Different germination times: radish 3–5 days, tomato 7–14 days.

slides.title: Sowing — step by step
bullets: Loosen soil to a forearm depth.
Mix in compost.
Make holes 2-finger-widths deep.
Drop 1–2 seeds; cover lightly; water gently.
Mark each row with a wooden tag.

slides.title: Water + weed + mulch
bullets: Water early morning or late afternoon.
Touch the soil first — if moist, skip a day.
Weed once a week; pull by the roots.
Mulch with dry leaves — keeps soil moist and cool.
Healthy soil = healthy plants.

slides.title: Pests and supports
bullets: Pests: caterpillars, aphids, snails.
Pick caterpillars off by hand.
Spray mild neem-water.
Plant marigolds nearby — natural deterrent.
Stake tall plants — tomato, brinjal — so they don't fall.

slides.title: Harvest and reflect
bullets: Spinach, coriander — pick large outer leaves.
Radish, carrot — pull when root is firm.
Tomato, brinjal, chilli — pluck when ripe.
Wash, share, save best seeds for next season.
Garden diary: 'what thrived? what struggled? what would I change?'

slides.title: You try (5 min)
bullets: 1. Sketch a 5×5 m Rabi garden.
2. List 5 tools you would need.
3. Where will tall plants go in your sketch?
4. Name 3 ways to start a plant.
5. Write 3 lines for your first garden-diary entry.

slides.title: Quick check
bullets: Q1. Best time to water?
Q2. Mint — direct sown or cutting?
Q3. Rabi — sow when?
Q4. Why mulch?
Show fingers.

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: A kitchen garden grows food; needs sun, soil, water, air, care.
Plan a sunny spot; pick a season (Kharif / Rabi / Zaid).
Tools: khurpi, trowel, watering can; soil + compost.
Three sowing methods: direct / seedlings / cuttings.
Care: water mornings; weed; mulch; pest-watch; stake.
Harvest carefully; save seeds; keep a garden diary.
